public_rationale: A preprint submitted May 23, 2026 reports operational power measurements from a 150 MW data center hosting 83,000 GB200 GPUs [e1]. This establishes that relevant GPU-equipped infrastructure was built, satisfying the limited construction condition, but does not identify its share of NVIDIA's 2025–2026 sales [e1]. NVIDIA reported $215.9 billion in total revenue for fiscal 2026, which ended January 25, 2026 [e2]. That company-wide fiscal figure does not measure calendar-year GPU purchases or equipment deployment dates [e2]. Neither item provides representative records connecting the relevant sales to widespread completed deployment, as required for early contradiction [e1] [e2].
limitations: The 2028–2029 forecast period remains future at the October 28, 2026 evaluation date.
The operating cluster is not matched to the relevant revenue recognition or shown to represent the broader sales cohort.
The packet does not quantify GPU purchases made years before use.
The claim leaves the fiscal/calendar convention and aggregate deployment threshold unspecified.
Total revenue includes products other than GPUs and does not establish commissioning dates.

statement.document_title: The AI Industry Is Lying To You

in some cases years in advance
will take until 2028 to 2029 to actually operationalize

our_interpretation: Operationalize means the purchased equipment is installed in powered facilities and performing computing work.
Read the forecast as describing deployment of the sales cohort in aggregate. It does not explicitly say that no individual GPU can operate earlier.
Use calendar 2025 and 2026 as a provisional reading of the unqualified years. Preserve the fiscal/calendar ambiguity rather than treating fiscal 2026 revenue as calendar 2026 revenue.
The exact words describe the construction rate as the basis for the prediction; they do not explicitly require that the rate remain unchanged through 2029.

The explicit construction antecedent is met if relevant GPU-equipped AI facilities are actually built. Evidence of one operating cluster satisfies that limited antecedent but cannot settle aggregate deployment timing.
criteria.support_condition: Matched sales and commissioning records show that deployment of the relevant 2025–2026 GPU sales cohort generally required waiting until 2028–2029, with the claimed advance-purchase spending independently documented.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative, value-weighted records establish that the relevant cohort was largely operational before 2028, or establish a materially different deployment timetable incompatible with the forecast.

evidence.explanation: Operational measurements establish that relevant GPU-equipped infrastructure existed by publication, satisfying the limited construction antecedent. The paper does not identify what share of NVIDIA's 2025–2026 recognized sales this cluster represents.
This is realized company-wide fiscal-year revenue. It is not calendar-year GPU spending, an installation count or evidence of when customers put the purchased equipment into operation.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative, value-weighted records linking 2025–2026 GPU sales and revenue recognition to installation and useful operation, with fiscal and calendar years distinguished. Deployment generally delayed until 2028–2029, alongside documented advance purchases, would support the claim. A materially incompatible timetable would contradict it. Before 2028, contradiction requires representative evidence of widespread completed deployment.
